activities.caption: rebuild the life framework, step by step
activities.name: budLifeOrder

config.prompt: The thin history scholars treat as factual — put the framework in order:
items: Born a prince in the Shakya republic (c. 480–400 BCE by recent scholarship)
Renounced household life; trained with meditation teachers
Years of austerity — abandoned as failure
Awakening under a tree, at about thirty-five
Roughly forty-five years teaching; a monastic order open across caste lines
Died at Kushinagar, leaving no successor — 'be a lamp unto yourselves'
config.why: The rich biography — the shielded palace, the four sights, the temptation by Mara — emerges centuries later in shaped texts: the tradition's own teaching instrument, dramatising the problem of dukkha.

activities.anchor: lays out the classic medical structure
activities.caption: pair each truth with its medical role
activities.name: budTruthsMatch

config.prompt: The first sermon's four truths, in the medical shape — pair term and role:

pairs.right: unsatisfactoriness threading even pleasure — birth, aging, sickness, death
craving (tanha): thirst for pleasure, existence, non-existence
cessation is possible — nirvana, literally 'blowing out', not annihilation
the Noble Eightfold Path, the middle way: wisdom, ethics, mental training

config.why: The path is simultaneous, not sequential — a whole life reoriented at once. And dukkha comes in three grades, the third being the chronic strain of holding together a self that is process pretending to be substance.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the category verdict
activities.name: budCategorySpot

config.prompt: One line of this 'philosophy or religion?' verdict is wrong — click it:
lines: The Buddha is not a creator, and insisted he was a human who woke up.
Devotional practice toward Buddha images is marginal across Asia — a purely Western habit.
Cosmology, ritual, monasticism, relics and pilgrimage are all present.
'Philosophy or religion?' is the category question failing on contact with the data.
Buddhism is a soteriology — a system aimed at transforming the person.
config.correction: Devotional practice toward Buddha images is central across Asia — merit, refuge, aspiration.
config.why: Which is exactly why the 'philosophy not religion' label fails: the tradition carries the full apparatus, and it aims at transformation — a soteriology.

config.text: Analysis of experience finds five aggregates — %%0%%, feeling, perception, mental formations and %%1%% — each impermanent (%%2%%), none a possessor; the self is a process, and clinging to it is the engine of dukkha.
config.hint: The first blank is the physical aggregate; the last is awareness itself; the Pali term means 'impermanent'.

activities.caption: file the marks of each vehicle
activities.name: budVehiclesSort

config.prompt: One diagnosis, three vehicles — file each mark:

items.label: the Pali Canon; the arhat ideal; Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand
monks on alms-round at dawn — the village-monastery symbiosis
the bodhisattva vow — awaken for the sake of all beings
China, Korea, Japan, Vietnam; the Lotus Sutra; Amitabha's Pure Land
Tibet, Bhutan, Mongolia; tantric technique — mantra, mandala, deity yoga
reincarnate lamas, including the Dalai Lamas

config.why: Each culture then remade the teaching — Chan/Zen, Pure Land piety, Nichiren's chanting, state Buddhism in Tibet: dozens of civilisations, one diagnosis.

config.prompt: At ordination a Theravada monk undertakes the full rulebook. About how many rules does the Vinaya set for a monk?
config.why: 227 — with the robe and alms-bowl unchanged for two and a half millennia. Laypeople keep the five precepts; the two-way economy trades material support for merit and teaching.
config.context: For comparison: the lay precepts the lesson lists are five.

activities.anchor: with human birth the fortunate middle
activities.caption: the poisoned arrow — you decide
activities.name: budArrowBranch

config.root: A man lies struck by an arrow. Before letting anyone treat him, he demands to know the archer's caste, his height, the bow's wood, the fletching's feather. The Buddha tells this parable about metaphysical questions. Play it out:

start.text: The ultimate questions press — who made the cosmos, is it eternal? Do you insist on answers first?

choices.label: Answers first — trace the arrow to its maker
choices.feedback: The parable's verdict: the person would die before the answers arrived — the questions stay open, and so does the wound.

choices.label: Treatment first — take up the path
choices.feedback: Liberation first; cosmology may wait. The Buddha's stance on speculation is itself doctrine, not evasion.

speculate.text: Every answer opens two more questions. Meanwhile the poison works. That is why the tradition's universe has no creator at its head: the cosmos is beginningless, running on karma's causality — there is no maker to trace.

practice.text: The path is walked, and the questions may be taken up later from a very different vantage. Even the gods attend sermons and seek teachings — they need the path too.

config.why: Gods abound in the texts, but they are mortal, samsaric, and none commands worship as the source of liberation — the precise claim is 'no creator', not 'no gods'.

config.prompt: Two centuries, two very different doors of entry — drag the divider:

before.label: The 1800s
before.text: Colonial philology edits and translates the Pali texts; Theosophical enthusiasm and converts like Henry Steel Olcott build a rationalist, anti-ritual 'Protestant Buddhism' — a lens that reshaped Asian self-understanding too.

after.label: Post-1950
after.text: Immigrant communities (Chinese, Vietnamese, Tibetan — the Dalai Lama's 1959 exile) and convert lineages (Zen, vipassana, Tibetan); Kabat-Zinn's MBSR (1979) delivers the breath-and-bodywork with the metaphysics stripped.

config.why: Scholars debate whether the clinical export is a newest vehicle or a derivative product — practitioners on both sides find the question clearer than the answer.
